items.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023
items.q: But this was Buddy Rich and he was playing at Lennie’s on the Turnpike, he’s going to be there for one week, I better take advantage of the moment and come up with something. So I wrote “Chelsea Bridge” for him

ctx.x: Ta-da. You know that was like a hot chart and still is of course. And I remember playing it and I was and still am a huge Cannonball Adderley fan so when it got to that part in your arrangement where it abruptly changed keys I was like whoa — what was that?

That was my first rock chart. And I’m sitting there — Buddy really wanted to do that. It was his doing. Cannonball had that album, the single rather, and it was kind of like a church scene if you remember. It was rumored — and I’m — he said that’s the only — I wrote three in one week which is for me unheard of. But this was Buddy Rich and he was playing at Lennie’s on the Turnpike, he’s going to be there for one week, I better take advantage of the moment and come up with something. So I wrote “Chelsea Bridge”…

And the “Chelsea Bridge,” that’s right, “Lush Life,” and “Mercy.” And the last one — actually I wasn’t used to the straight eighth notes at the time [scats] and writing all those damn things out, which takes some time. And so [scats] You know? And then there’s that celebratory kind of sound, you know [scats].
